claims.statement: `GET /accounts/holdings` paginates positions, not accounts or holdings rows: `PositionRepository.get_by_user` counts `PositionModel` rows joined to the user's `AccountModel` rows, so the response `total` is a position count and one account can contribute several items whose rows may be split across page boundaries because the service only ever regroups the fetched page.

`PositionService.get_user_holdings` buckets the repository's page by `account_id`, resolves each distinct account once through `AccountService.get_account` (not once per position), converts each position via `_calculate_holdings`, and then layers account context onto the already-converted rows with `UserHoldingRead(**holding.model_dump(), account_id=account.id, account_name=account.name)`.

`PositionService.get_account_holdings` computes `total_value` and `total_profit_loss` over every position of the account (an unlimited `get_by_account` call) while returning only one paginated page of `items`, and when `account.net_deposits` is set it recomputes `total_profit_loss` as `total_value - Money(net_deposits, account.currency)` with `total_profit_loss_percent` only when `net_deposits != 0`.

`HoldingRead` carries both native-currency values (`average_cost`, `unconverted_total_value`, `unconverted_profit_loss`, `security_currency`) and account-currency values (`total_value`, `profit_loss`, `currency`, `converted_average_cost`, `converted_latest_price`), plus identity and price metadata (`id`, `security_id`, `security_symbol`, `security_name`, `latest_price`, `price_date`, `updated_at`); `UserHoldingRead` adds `account_id`/`account_name` and `AccountHoldingsRead` extends `PaginatedResponse[HoldingRead]` with account identity, totals, `total_profit_loss_percent`, `net_deposits`, `free_cash` and `currency`.

Authorization differs per holdings endpoint: `GET /accounts/holdings` is scoped implicitly by the repository's join on `AccountModel.user_id`, whereas `GET /accounts/{account_id}/holdings` and `GET /accounts/{account_id}/totals` look the account up and call `authorization_api.check_entity_owned_by_user` before delegating to `PositionService`.

`_calculate_holdings` silently skips a position whose security cannot be resolved (it logs "Security not found for position ..." and continues), so a holdings page can return fewer rows than the position count in `total`.

`PositionService.get_holdings_by_security` fills the repository's `AccountHoldingRead` placeholder rows (`total_value=0.0`, `currency=""`) with `quantity × latest close` in the security currency, `account_total_value` from `get_total_for_account` and `account_percentage` only when the account total is positive, and returns an ambiguous `([], 0)` when the security is unknown — behaviour the source marks with a TODO.

The `/holdings` load reads preferences, portfolios and the account list in one `Promise.allSettled` and returns exactly seven keys — `holdings_table_config`, `group_mode`, `elliott_waves`, `portfolios`, `accounts`, `portfolio_id` and `account_id` — falling back to `normalizeHoldingsTableConfig(null)`, `normalizeHoldingsGroupMode(null)`, `null` waves and empty arrays for any non-401 rejection; it never awaits or returns holdings rows.

SSR requests pass the `auth_token` cookie explicitly as a Bearer override because `ApiClient.get` only sets `Authorization: Bearer` when a token override is supplied (it always sets `credentials: 'include'`); the `/`, `/accounts/[id]` and `/holdings` loads map a 401 from their awaited requests to `deleteAuthCookie` plus a 303 redirect to `/auth/login?clear_session=true` (`/holdings` detects it by inspecting each `Promise.allSettled` result and re-throwing the 303 through its `catch`), other `ApiError` statuses in the two single-request loads to Kit errors and anything else to a 500, while the `/holdings` post-navigation 401 is routed through `redirectOn401`, which `goto`s `/auth/login?clear_session=true` without deleting the httpOnly cookie client-side (`hooks.server.ts` clears it when the login page resolves).

`/holdings` derives its header totals by bucketing `service.rows` on `row.currency` in a `SvelteMap`: it sums `total_value`, sums non-null `profit_loss` (tracking `hasProfitLoss`), accumulates `costBasis` as `quantity × (converted_average_cost ?? average_cost ?? 0)` only when positive, and computes `returnPercent` only when `costBasis > 0` — values are never summed across currency buckets.

`groupHoldings` in `stock` mode (and its legacy `company` alias) keys strictly on `security_id`, keeps first-appearance ordering, sums `quantity`/`total_value`/`unconverted_total_value` and null-preserving P/L, computes quantity-weighted `average_cost` and `converted_average_cost`, dedupes `account_names` and counts distinct accounts — and hardcodes the group `currency` to `'CAD'`, so values already converted into different account currencies are summed under a CAD label.

The `/holdings` page owns its `HoldingsService` instance instead of reading a layout context: it constructs the service, seeds the group mode with `setGroupBy(data.group_mode)`, seeds the account/portfolio filter from `data.portfolio_id`/`data.account_id` in an effect, and triggers `service.load()` from a single `$effect` so the rows arrive after navigation; toggling grouping is therefore a pure client-side derivation that never refetches holdings, and `getHoldingsService` remains the context/custom-fetch accessor for other callers.

`HoldingsService.load()` is the sole implementation of the collect-every-page contract: it loops `getUserHoldings(offset, PAGE_SIZE, token)` sequentially with `PAGE_SIZE = 50` and the `MAX_PAGES = 100` stale-total cap, breaks early on an empty page, toggles `isLoading` around the whole loop, never throws (it stores the message in `errorMessage`, keeps the previously loaded rows, and returns the caught error or `null`), clears the error on the next success, and — after the loop — issues at most one non-fatal `getValuationsBatch` for the distinct `security_id`s inside its own `try/catch` that degrades to an empty `valuations` map.

`holdings-table.svelte` stays presentational: it derives a normalized `HoldingsTableConfig` from the `tableConfig` prop, keeps a local copy so a column drag gives immediate feedback, and emits the final clamped config once at pointer-up via `onConfigChange`, while the `/holdings` page owns persistence and pushes write failures into a `holdings-error` alert without reverting the optimistic UI change.

`holdings_table` and `holdings_group` are persisted one top-level key at a time (`patchPreferences({ holdings_table: config })` / `patchPreferences({ holdings_group: mode })`) through an injected structural prefs service instead of the module singleton, matching the backend's top-level JSONB `||` merge so a concurrent write to a different preference key cannot be dropped (nested values of the same key remain last-write-wins).

`normalizeHoldingsTableConfig` guarantees a usable config from any stored shape: non-object/missing input yields defaults, unknown column ids are dropped from `widths` and `visible`, widths are clamped by `clampColumnWidth` (non-finite → default), surviving `visible` ids are re-ordered to canonical `HOLDINGS_TABLE_COLUMN_IDS` order with the sticky column force-included, an empty or fully invalid `visible` list falls back to all columns, and the returned object never aliases the defaults.

`HOLDINGS_TABLE_STICKY_COLUMN_ID` (`security_symbol`) can never be hidden: `toggleColumnVisibility` returns the same config object unchanged for it, the display-settings menu item is `disabled`, and the table uses the constant for its sticky cell and skeleton columns, while `normalizeHoldingsTableConfig` re-adds it to any stored `visible` list.

`normalizeHoldingsGroupMode` normalizes the persisted `holdings_group` value to `'stock'` only for `'stock'` and the legacy `'company'`, and to `'none'` for every other value (including `'STOCK'`, numbers, objects and `null`), so a stored legacy mode still renders grouped while the next save writes `'stock'`.

`AccountClient.getAccountHoldings(id, token)` sends no `offset`/`limit`, so `/accounts/[id]` receives the backend defaults (offset 0, limit 50 for `PaginationParams`) while `AccountHoldingsRead.total` and the header totals cover every position of the account — meaning accounts with more than 50 positions render truncated rows next to complete totals.

The accounts dashboard `/` reads only the account list (`GET /accounts/`, ordered by account name) in its server load and defers each row's value to a client-side `GET /accounts/{id}/totals` call that `PositionService.get_total_for_account` resolves by pricing the account's positions, converting into the account currency (plus converted free cash) and returning `AccountTotals` (`cost`/`value` as `Money`); the per-item state caches the result and invalidates it when a sync finishes, and the dashboard itself renders no holdings rows.

`/accounts/[id]` renders its header from `AccountHoldingsRead` and its body through the separate presentational `frontend/src/lib/components/accounts/holdings-table.svelte`, which takes `holdings` and `totalAccountValue`, has no column configuration or grouping, shows native- and account-currency values side by side when they differ, and is mounted only when `data.holdings.items.length > 0`.

The holdings read path's test suites follow the repository's mocking contract: the frontend suites mock every API client and framework module that performs network or browser work (`$lib/api/accountService`, `$lib/api/marketService`, `$lib/api/userPreferencesService`, `$lib/api/portfolioClient`, `$lib/api/accountClient`, `$lib/server/auth-cookie`, `$app/paths`, `$app/navigation`) and never call the backend, pinning the preference/portfolio/account-only load and its paging absence, the `HoldingsService` paging loop, stale-total guards, batch-valuation degradation and filter derivation, per-currency bucketing, grouping toggles, the `redirectOn401` path and single-key preference writes; the backend suites mock `PositionRepository`, `AccountService`, `SecurityApi` and `MarketPricesApi` and pin user isolation, pagination and per-account stamping.

The `/holdings` read path is split into three phases: the SSR load returns only the preference- and filter-context-derived keys (and a test asserts `getUserHoldings` is never called from the load), the browser-only `$effect` then drives `HoldingsService.load()` to page every position and fetch one batch valuation, and user interactions afterwards issue single-key `PATCH /accounts/me/preferences` writes and `goto`-only URL/filter updates — so the shell paints skeletons before any holdings request and the page survives a failed load with an in-page `holdings-error` alert.

The two account-scoped totals paths use different P&L bases: `_calculate_holdings` produces cost-basis P&L (`value − quantity × average_cost`) and that is what the `/holdings` header approximates client-side, whereas `get_account_holdings` overwrites `total_profit_loss` with the cash-flow figure `total_value − Money(net_deposits, account.currency)` (with `total_profit_loss_percent` over `net_deposits` when non-zero) as soon as `account.net_deposits` is set, so deposits and withdrawals move the account page's header without any position changing.

The `/holdings` SSR load's three requests are settled independently: every `Promise.allSettled` result is inspected for an `ApiError` with status 401, which triggers `deleteAuthCookie(cookies)` and a 303 redirect (re-thrown through the load's `catch`), while any other rejection is tolerated — a preferences outage leaves the normalized defaults and a portfolio or account-list outage leaves an empty array, so the page still renders and the filter dropdown simply has fewer options.

`HoldingsService` splits fetched rows into `allRows` and a derived `rows` getter over a `HoldingsFilter` (`all`, `portfolio` with its account ids, or `account`), with `filterByPortfolio` / `filterByAccount` / `clearFilter` replacing the filter; filtering is therefore a pure client-side derivation (no refetch) that also drives `groupedHoldings` and the page's per-currency header totals, and the page mirrors the selection into the URL via `goto('/holdings?portfolio_id=…' | '/holdings?account_id=…' | '/holdings', { replaceState: true })` from the header filter dropdown or an account-badge click.

The holdings table's account column renders one interactive account badge per account rather than a plain name, each carrying that row's share of the account's own value (`calculatePercentOfAccount`), the row's share of the currently displayed portfolio value is exposed as the `percent_of_total` column (`calculatePercentOfTotal` over the visible rows, so the denominator follows the active filter), and the newest `valuation_range` column projects the `valuations` map into a two-bound range with the midpoint used for sorting and an em dash for unvalued securities.

The holdings table's header controls are consolidated into a single icon-only `display-settings-trigger` dropdown that holds both the "Group by stock" checkbox (`group-by-stock`, checked for `'stock'` or `'company'`) and one `column-toggle-{id}` item per entry in `HOLDINGS_TABLE_COLUMNS`, with the sticky column's item `disabled`; there is no standalone group checkbox or column-visibility trigger.

`GET /accounts/{account_id}/holdings` accepts the shared `PaginationParams` dependency, so the router route can page an account's positions, but the frontend's `AccountClient.getAccountHoldings(id, token)` sends no `offset`/`limit`, leaving the backend defaults (`offset = 0`, `limit = 50`) in effect while `AccountHoldingsRead.total` and the header totals cover every position of the account.
